# Lisbon 5-Day Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A balanced Lisbon trip for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14** with a **€1,800 total budget excluding flights** is very workable. I’ve kept it walkable, mixed in museums and food, and built in **one easy day trip** with a pace check on each day.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary and Spend

### Day 1: Baixa, Chiado, and Alfama first look
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and do a gentle walk through **Baixa** and **Rossio**.
- Afternoon: Visit **MUDE** or the **Lisbon Story Centre**, then wander into **Chiado** for cafés and bookshops.
- Evening: Sunset in **Alfama** and a relaxed fado dinner.
- Estimated spend: **€210–€260**
- Pace check: **Comfortable**; good arrival-day rhythm.

### Day 2: Museums and riverside walking
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** for a strong art focus.
- Afternoon: Lunch in **Saldanha** or **Avenidas Novas**, then visit **MAAT** or the **National Coach Museum** depending on interest.
- Evening: Easy riverside walk in **Belém** with pasteis stop.
- Estimated spend: **€220–€290**
- Pace check: **Moderate**; museum-heavy but still manageable.

### Day 3: Easy day trip to Sintra
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- Morning: Early train to **Sintra**.
- Afternoon: Choose **one main site** only, such as **Pena Palace** or **Quinta da Regaleira**, plus a short town stroll.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/aa/Palacio_Nacional_da_Pena%2C_Sintra%2C_Portugal%2C_2019-05-25%2C_DD_125.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Choose **one main site** only, such as **Pena Palace** or **Quinta da Regaleira**, plus a short town stroll, Lisbon, Portugal
- Evening: Return to Lisbon for a simple dinner near your hotel.
- Estimated spend: **€180–€260**
- Pace check: **Good if limited to one major attraction**; can get rushed if you try to do too much.

### Day 4: Belém, food stops, and a flexible neighborhood evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: **Jerónimos Monastery** and **Pastéis de Belém**.
- Afternoon: **Belém Tower** or a slower lunch-and-river break if you prefer less moving around.
- Evening: Head to **Príncipe Real** or **Cais do Sodré** for dinner and drinks.
- Estimated spend: **€200–€280**
- Pace check: **Comfortable**; a good reset day after Sintra.

### Day 5: Local market, final shopping, and departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: **Time Out Market** or a local breakfast in **Graça**.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/83/Lobster%2C_Time_Out_Market_Lisboa_%2850661858143%29.jpg Alt=Morning: **Time Out Market** or a local breakfast in **Graça**, Lisbon, Portugal
- Afternoon: Final shopping in **Chiado** or a viewpoint stroll if your departure is later.
- Evening: Depart.
- Estimated spend: **€120–€180**
- Pace check: **Easy**; leave this day light.

## Best Neighborhood Bases in Lisbon

### 1) Baixa / Chiado
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Best for: first-time visitors, walkability, easy transit
- Why it works: central, flat-ish in parts, close to museums, shopping, and dining
- Trade-off: can be pricier and busier than other areas

### 2) Príncipe Real / Bairro Alto edge
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Best for: cafés, restaurants, stylish stays, walkable evenings
- Why it works: good access to Chiado, Avenida da Liberdade, and central sights
- Trade-off: some nightlife noise in Bairro Alto itself

### 3) Alfama / Graça
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Best for: atmosphere, viewpoints, older Lisbon charm
- Why it works: scenic and memorable, with good local food options
- Trade-off: hills and stairs; less convenient with heavy luggage

## Recommended Stay Types and Budget Fit

| Stay Type | Typical 4 Nights for 2 | Best For | Budget Fit |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Boutique hotel in Baixa/Chiado | €700–€1,050 | easiest logistics | Strong |
| Apartment in Príncipe Real | €600–€950 | space + neighborhood feel | Strong |
| Guesthouse in Alfama/Graça | €500–€850 | character + value | Strong |

**Best match for your request:** a **boutique hotel in Baixa or Chiado** with **private bathroom** and **free cancellation**. That usually gives the smoothest mix of comfort, walkability, and transit access.

## Spending Plan for the Full Trip

- Lodging: **€600–€1,000**
- Food and drinks: **€420–€620**
- Museums and entry tickets: **€120–€220**
- Local transit and taxis: **€60–€120**
- Sintra day trip: **€100–€180**
- Buffer / snacks / extras: **€100–€180**

**Total estimated range:** **€1,400–€2,320**
**Targeted practical range:** **€1,650–€1,800** with midrange lodging and a moderate dining style.

## Days That Look Too Rushed

- **Day 3** can feel rushed if you try to combine **Pena Palace + Quinta da Regaleira + Moorish Castle**. Pick **one main site** and keep the rest light.
- **Day 2** can become museum-heavy if you add Belém and central Lisbon in the same afternoon. Keep one museum as the main focus.
- **Day 5** is only rushed if your departure is early; otherwise it should stay easy.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Find hotels] https://www.booking.com/city/pt/lisbon.html
Action: [Button: Check trains to Sintra] https://www.cp.pt/passageiros/en
Action: [Button: Lisbon museum passes] https://www.museusemonumentos.pt/

## Sources

- Lisbon official tourism: https://www.visitlisboa.com/
- CP trains to Sintra: https://www.cp.pt/passageiros/en
- Lisbon museums and monuments: https://www.museusemonumentos.pt/
- Booking Lisbon stays: https://www.booking.com/city/pt/lisbon.html
